question: What is probability, and which rules, distributions and simulation methods let you compute and reason about it?
contributions: Contrasts frequentist and Bayesian meanings of probability
States product, conditional, addition and Bayes rules with their caveats
Uses Monte Carlo simulation and worked puzzles (Monty Hall, Poincare, drug test) plus 17 exercises

limits: Only the first edition style: no formal axioms, no continuous-variable treatment beyond mentioning normal and binomial PMF
Monte Carlo is noted slow for rare events; 'a little bit of analysis can save a lot of computing'
Anecdotes (Poincare) flagged as probably fabricated; drug-test numbers are 1990s-era JAMA estimates
Exercises have no solutions in this chapter
Heights parameters (sigma^2 = 59.4 cm) have unit/variance-vs-sd ambiguity
practices: Check independence before multiplying probabilities; otherwise use P(A and B)=P(A)P(B|A) (Sec 5.1).
Use P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B) unless events are mutually exclusive (Sec 5.4).
Simulate a random system with Monte Carlo to judge whether an apparent streak or cluster is meaningful (Sec 5.6).
Read Bayes as prior x likelihood / normalizing constant, with P(E)=P(D)P(E|D)+P(N)P(E|N) (Sec 5.7).
Account for base rate when interpreting a positive test: sensitivity alone is not the posterior (Sec 5.7).
Compare variability across groups with the coefficient of variation sigma/mu (Sec 5.3 aside).

terms.definition: Something that may or may not occur, with some probability.
One in a series of occasions when an event might occur.
A strict interpretation of probability that only applies to a series of identical trials.
A more general interpretation that uses probability to represent a subjective degree of belief.
Two events are independent if the occurrence of one does has no effect on the probability of another.
A statistic that measures spread, normalized by central tendency, for comparison between distributions with different means.
A method of computing probabilities by simulating random processes.
A probability before a Bayesian update.
A probability computed by a Bayesian update.
The probability of the evidence conditioned on a hypothesis.
The denominator of Bayes's Theorem, used to normalize the result to be a probability.
Likely to produce a positive result if there are drugs in a sample (Sec 5.7).
Likely to yield a negative result if there are no drugs (Sec 5.7).
Reading Bayes's theorem as how the probability of a hypothesis gets updated over time in light of new evidence.
